record.paper_title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds: Main Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Threshold comparing Hopf and parallel-transport bounds
record.original_question: For each m > 1, define r1(m) as a threshold such that for r > r1(m) the Hopf vector fields of length r on S^{2m+1} have less volume than the parallel-transport vector fields used to produce the alternative upper bound c*(m,r) vol(S^{2m+1}). Determine explicit values or a formula for r1(m), and clarify its relation to the instability threshold r0(m) = sqrt(2m - 3).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m>1$ be an integer and consider the odd-dimensional unit sphere $S^{2m+1}\subset \mathbb{R}^{2m+2}$ endowed with its round metric. A smooth vector field $V$ of constant length $r>0$ on $S^{2m+1}$ may be viewed as a section of the tangent bundle, and its volume is defined as the $(2m+1)$-dimensional volume of its image in $TS^{2m+1}$ equipped with the Sasaki metric:
$$\operatorname{vol}(V)=\int_{S^{2m+1}}\sqrt{\det\bigl(I+(\nabla V)^{T}(\nabla V)\bigr)}\,d\mathrm{vol}.$$
For $r>0$ let $H_r$ denote a Hopf vector field of constant length $r$ on $S^{2m+1}$ (the unit Hopf field rescaled by $r$), and let $\operatorname{vol}(H_r)$ be its volume. There is an alternative upper bound for the infimum of $\operatorname{vol}(V)$ among constant-length-$r$ vector fields on $S^{2m+1}$ of the form
$$c^{*}(m,r)\,\operatorname{vol}(S^{2m+1}),$$
constructed via the family of parallel-transport vector fields (the vector field obtained, off a singular set, by parallel-transporting a fixed unit tangent vector along great circles, and then rescaling by $r$).

Define
$$r_1(m)=\inf\bigl\{\,r_0>0 : \operatorname{vol}(H_r)<c^{*}(m,r)\,\operatorname{vol}(S^{2m+1}) \text{ for all } r>r_0\bigr\}.$$
That is, $r_1(m)$ is the threshold above which the Hopf vector fields of length $r$ have strictly smaller volume than the parallel-transport upper bound. It is known that the Hopf vector field $H_r$ becomes unstable (as a critical point of the volume functional on constant-length sections) when $r>r_0(m):=\sqrt{2m-3}$.

Determine an explicit value or closed-form formula for $r_1(m)$ as a function of $m$, and determine its precise relation to $r_0(m)=\sqrt{2m-3}$ (in particular whether $r_1(m)\le r_0(m)$, $r_1(m)=r_0(m)$, or $r_1(m)>r_0(m)$).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicitly open question in the survey on volumes of vector fields on Riemannian manifolds, where it is stated that the explicit values of r_1(m) are not known and its relationship with the instability threshold r_0(m)=sqrt(2m-3) remains to be clarified. No subsequent resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: The Volume of Vector Fields on Riemannian Manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: We don't know the explicit values of r_1(m)
status_evidence.claim: Authors state explicitly that the threshold r_1(m) is unknown.
